items.title: Suspect in attempted jewelry store heist near Niagara Falls, Ontario nabbed in Mississauga
items.summary: A late October attempted break-and-enter at a jewelry store near Niagara Falls has led four weeks later to the arrest of a Brampton man in Mississauga, police say. Niagara Regional Police said the wanted man was collared by Peel Regional Police on Monday and is now in custody pending a court appearance. A second man wanted in connection with the incident is currently in the custody of another police service and will be turned over to Niagara police once he’s released, investigators said. Both men are suspects in the Oct. 26 attempted break-and-enter at a jewelry store in the area of Thorold Road and Prince Charles Drive in Welland, southwest of Niagara Falls. m. that day, according to police, a white Volkswagen Touareg SUV was used to hit the front of the business in an attempt to gain access. “The suspects were unable to gain access and fled the scene in a black Audi Q7 SUV at a high rate of speed prior to police arrival,” Niagara police said in a news release on Tuesday. Initial investigation determined that two masked male culprits were involved, detectives noted. Police said earlier that no injuries were reported and that the building sustained significant damages. A structural engineer was consulted to determine the integrity of the building, they added.

items.title: Two people injured in police cruiser crash in Mississauga
items.summary: Two people were injured after a collision involving a police cruiser in Mississauga on Monday night. , Peel Regional Police said. Police said two people, the driver and passenger, were transported to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. They were later released from hospital, police added. The officer was not injured, police said. Dixie Road was closed, but has since reopened. UPDATE Roadway has been opened Driver and passenger have been medically assessed and released from hospital.

items.title: Second Officer Tells Francique Inquest Surveillance, Not a Planned Arrest, Was Underway That Night
items.summary: According to testimony at the coroner's inquest into the death of Jamal Francique, Det. Mani Sharifi said police had no plan to arrest Francique on the night he was fatally shot in 2020. Sharifi told the inquest officers moved in only after they observed Francique breaching his bail conditions by leaving his home. The real plan, Sharifi said, was to continue surveillance that had already been underway for roughly three or four days until an opportunity arose. A juror asked why Francique was not arrested earlier in the week, once officers first saw him breach his bail, and Sharifi said his unit was instead focused on investigating whether Francique possessed a firearm or was involved in drug activity. Francique was shot by an officer outside a Mississauga townhouse complex on the evening of Jan. 7, 2020, according to the inquest.

items.title: Dixie Road Shut Down in Both Directions After Crash Involving a Police Cruiser
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Paramedic Services, one person was taken to hospital with minor, non-life threatening injuries after a two-vehicle collision involving a police cruiser in Mississauga on Monday night. Paramedics say the crash happened on Dixie Road north of Rathburn Road. The other driver involved remained at the scene, paramedics said. Dixie Road is currently closed in both directions between Rathburn Road and Burnhamthorpe Road while crews respond, according to police. Police are asking motorists to seek alternate routes while the road remains closed.

items.title: Rooftop Solar and Two EVs Help Mississauga Couple Cut Energy Bills Well Below National Average
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, Mississauga residents Harminder Dhillon and Jyoti Grewal say they spent roughly $1,100 in 2025 to power their home and run two electric vehicles. The couple installed rooftop solar panels, disconnected natural gas service, switched to heat pumps and an induction stove, and replaced gas powered cars with electric ones, bringing their reported costs to about $92 a month. Canadian households spent an average of $4,943 on energy in 2023, according to Natural Resources Canada's Energy Fact Book. The outlet notes the figures come from different years and are not a direct comparison, since energy costs vary with home size and local rates. Dhillon, an engineer turned criminal lawyer, says the switch began as a response to climate change rather than an effort to save money, describing it to CityNews as a climate decision, not a financial one.

items.title: Mississauga Residents Can Begin Booking Winter Recreation Programs and March Break Camps Tuesday
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga residents can begin registering Tuesday morning for the city's winter recreation and culture programs as well as March break camps. The City of Mississauga says registration opens earlier for residents than for non-residents, who must wait a few weeks longer to sign up. City officials describe winter as a good time to learn something new, stay active and connect with the community, and say the programs are offered to residents of all ages, interests and abilities. Residents can create a wish list of programs online ahead of registration, which the city says helps when trying to secure a spot in popular offerings that fill up quickly. In-person registration is also available at community centres during service desk hours, according to the city.

items.title: City of Mississauga to implement hiring restrictions effective immediately
items.summary: One week into the term of Mississauga's new mayor and hiring restrictions are going into effect at the city. It comes after staff were directed by Mayor Alvin Tedjo to freeze property taxes for the 2027 and 2028 budgets.

items.title: Car Insurance ON Mississauga
items.summary: In 2026, the average car insurance premium in Mississauga is $3,078 per year (about $257 per month). 01% higher than the provincial average of $2,653. This makes Mississauga 176th out of 181 Ontario communities for car insurance affordability. As of July 1, 2026 in Ontario, some previously mandatory accident benefits are now optional. ca data, drivers in Mississauga pay about $3,078 per year for auto insurance as of March 2026. Drivers here pay premiums that are higher than in Burlington, which is the cheapest city for car insurance in the GTA at $2,109 per year. However, insurance costs in Mississauga are lower relative to the premiums in Brampton, the most expensive city in the region at $3,802 per year. Nearby Oakville has an average premium of $2,167 per year ($181 per month), which is $911 less than Mississauga. Car insurance premiums depend on many factors, such as the number of claims in an area, the amount of time drivers spend on the road, and each driver’s personal and insurance history. The lowest average premium in Mississauga is found in the L5J area, where drivers pay $2,737 annually. Meanwhile, drivers in L4T have the highest average premiums at $3,937 per year.

items.title: Mississauga Ward 10 Councillor to Host Virtual Town Hall on Lisgar Beaver Problem
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga Ward 10 Coun. Sue McFadden says the city will hold a virtual town hall on Jan. 13 to explain its strategy for managing beavers disrupting water flow in the city's northwest end. Officials plan to outline efforts to keep the animals from causing further problems in the Lisgar community, near the Milton border. The city removed several beaver dams and relocated beavers from around Sixteen Mile Creek and Osprey Marsh last fall and winter after the dams caused drainage issues, according to the report. Despite that removal effort, residents reported seeing beavers back in the area by spring, prompting McFadden to promise closer monitoring. McFadden says beavers, among the largest rodents in the world, continue to live along Sixteen Mile Creek, and another lodge and series of dams have recently been spotted further north within the tributary.

items.title: Helicopter Tracks Driver Going Over 200 km/h Through Mississauga and Brampton to an Arrest
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, a driver was clocked travelling more than 200 km/h on Mississauga and Brampton streets and highways in an incident officers tied to the recent release of Grand Theft Auto VI. Police released video showing the vehicle speeding through both cities before reaching the highway, say officers. Air3, the force's helicopter unit, tracked the vehicle from above until officers located it at a residence and made an arrest, police say. Peel police used the stop as what they called a cheeky example of what not to do on the roads, reminding residents that unlike the video game, there are no respawns or reset buttons in real life. Officers say the message was simple, keep the speeding, stunts and getaway drives in the game, not on Mississauga's roads.

items.title: Peel, Halton police launch annual Miracle on Main Street campaign ahead of holiday season
items.summary: Police in Peel and Halton regions launched their annual Miracle on Main Street campaign Monday, which seeks to provide toy, gift card and essential item donations for families in need.
